summary: Redwood hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming responses, key parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop), and retry/idempotency patterns. Customer interested in hosted first with a potential Dedicated POC; main concerns: latency SLOs, cost, and data residency. Next: share pricing, streaming snippets, and customer will provide prompt set for evaluation.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on your account. With me is Arjun our SE. Quick intros?
[00:00:10] Maya: Hi Lena, Maya Chen, CTO at ByteWave. We've got Ravi on the ML side, Sara product, Jordan infrastructure.
[00:00:20] Ravi: Hi.
[00:00:22] Arjun: Great, thanks. High level, we want to show how our Hosted API handles chat and text gen  streaming, common params, and recommended retry patterns. We'll also touch briefly on the Console and Optimize tips.
[00:00:35] Jordan: Sounds good. Our main things: latency under 300ms for short responses, cost predictability, and SSO.
[00:00:42] Lena: Perfect. We'll keep that in mind.
[00:00:50] Arjun: Alright, jumping in. Quick architecture slide  hosted API is a simple REST + SDK interface. Example: POST /v1/generate or /v1/chat with model param. You can stream tokens via SSE or websocket; streaming reduces perceived latency for tokens as they arrive instead of waiting for final output.
[00:01:10] [00:01:12] Arjun: Demo time  I'll share my screen and call the API from the Node SDK. Code snippet (rough, live):
  const res = await client.chat.create({
    model: 'rw-instruct-1',
    messages: [{role: 'system', content: 'You are a helpful assistant'}, {role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the quarterly metrics.'}],
    stream: true, // enable streaming
    temperature: 0.2,
    max_tokens: 250
  });
[00:01:45] Arjun: As the response streams, you'll see chunked events. In Node we wire up an event listener: res.on('data', chunk => { process.stdout.write(chunk) })  that way frontend shows tokens immediately.
[00:02:00] Sara: Is streaming compatible with our current websocket infra? We use server-sent events in some places.
[00:02:07] Arjun: Yes, we support SSE and websockets; browser fetch streaming works too. Keep in mind the SDK provides helpers to reassemble deltas.
[00:02:15] Maya: Any rate-limit implications with streaming?
[00:02:18] Arjun: Good Q. Streaming counts same token units as non-streaming for billing. Rate limits are per-tenant and configurable; for hosted plans we enforce per-second token-in and request QPS. If you expect high bursty traffic, we recommend batching or a higher quota. For Dedicated you can set higher reserved throughput.
[00:02:40] [00:02:42] Lena: On parameters  common knobs we recommend: temperature (0 1), top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, presence/ frequency penalties. For deterministic outputs we drop temperature toward 0 and set a tight top_p.
[00:02:58] Ravi: Do you have guidance on temperature vs top_p tradeoffs for summarization vs creative copy?
[00:03:05] Arjun: Summarization  low temp 0 0.2, top_p 0.9 1.0; creative  temp 0.7+, top_p 0.9 maybe lower. For scoring/rerank, use beam-like lower temp.
[00:03:18] [00:03:20] Sara: How to enforce output length? Sometimes it overflows.
[00:03:23] Arjun: Use max_tokens to cap generation and add stop tokens. For structured outputs, we recommend function/tool calling or schema validation on client side. Also prefix instruction like "Respond in 3 bullet points" helps.
[00:03:35] Jordan: Ok but if a stream gets cut due to network, how do we handle retries without getting duplicate responses?
[00:03:42] Arjun: We recommend idempotency keys for request-level idempotency. The pattern: client sends idempotency key header (Idempotency-Key: <uuid>). On retry, server recognizes completed or in-progress requests and either returns cached output or dedupes. For partial streams, you can resume by requesting from last token index if you're on a Dedicated plan with KV cache enabled, otherwise best to retry with same key and use server-side dedupe.
[00:04:08] Maya: Does Redwood support resume tokens or partial KV cache for hosted?
[00:04:11] Arjun: Hosted has prefix caching for repeated prefixes, but fine-grained resume is more of a Dedicated capability where we expose KV-cache hooks.
[00:04:21] [00:04:22] Ravi: What about exponential backoff recommendations?
[00:04:24] Arjun: Typical: detect transient 429/503, backoff with jitter, and retry 3 times. For idempotent calls, it's safe; for non-idempotent you must use idempotency-key. We have SDK helpers  sample code I will share.
[00:04:37] Lena: Also note the retry/inflight best practice to avoid amplifying cost: add a short client-side timeout shorter than server's long-running default to fail fast.
[00:04:46] Sara: Can you show the Console for per-route metrics quickly?
[00:04:50] Arjun: Yep, switching to Console. Here is the per-model dashboard  token breakdown by request, latency percentile graphs, cost estimates. You can set per-route budgets and autoscale configs.
[00:05:05] [00:05:07] Arjun: Under Optimize, we show recommended quantization or batching suggestions based on your traffic profile. For example, if you have many short 1 2 message chats, we recommend aggressive batching and prefix caching to reduce unit cost.
[00:05:20] Jordan: How do we test latencies? Can we share a synthetic load?
[00:05:24] Lena: Yes, for POC we often run a benchmark with your prompt set and desired QPS. We'll spin a small benchmark, measure p50/p95, and recommend hosted configs or Dedicated sizing.
[00:05:34] Maya: Let's talk security briefly  SSO and audit logs.
[00:05:37] Arjun: Hosted supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. Data at rest encryption and KMS integrations for Private deployments; on Hosted we provide SOC2 reports and can discuss contractual data handling.
[00:05:50] Ravi: Do you store prompts/outputs by default? We need retention options.
[00:05:53] Lena: By default, logs are stored for some retention but we have options: short retention, disable retention for sensitive workloads, or Private deployment where you control storage. We'll include that in the security doc pack.
[00:06:05] [00:06:07] Sara: About cost  if we do lots of streaming, is there a hidden cost?
[00:06:10] Arjun: Streaming itself doesn't add extra cost beyond token counts, but you might pay more tokens due to repeated re-sends on retries if you don't dedupe. Also long-running streams might increase connection usage; for very high scale we discuss Dedicated.
[00:06:22] Maya: Practical question: do you have sample retry code for client-side network blips?
[00:06:26] Arjun: Yes, I'll share. Example pattern in Python using backoff lib and idempotency header. I'll attach the snippet in Slack/Email.
[00:06:36] [00:06:38] Arjun: Demo wrap-up: live stream showed token-by-token delivery, how to adjust temperature/top_p, and idempotency guidance.
[00:06:45] Jordan: One more thing  data residency. We need EU-only for some endpoints.
[00:06:49] Lena: We can provision regionally-hosted endpoints. For Hosted we have EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Private. We'll include the infra options in the follow-up.
[00:06:59] Sara: Any common pitfalls?
[00:07:02] Arjun: A few: 1) Not using stop tokens so you get overruns. 2) Retries without idempotency keys. 3) Assuming streaming reduces billing (it doesn't). 4) Overly aggressive temperature causing hallucinations.
[00:07:16] Ravi: Good list.
[00:07:18] Lena: Ok let's do quick Q&A  Ravi?
[00:07:22] Ravi: For fine-tuning or instruction tuning, do you recommend hosted vs bring-your-own model?
[00:07:27] Arjun: Hosted supports a set of verified models; for custom fine-tuning we have options: host custom variants in Dedicated or bring your own model to Private. If you need to keep data in-house for training, Private is best.
[00:07:39] Maya: What SLA can we expect for Hosted?
[00:07:41] Lena: Hosted has a best-effort SLA; Dedicated comes with an SLA and guaranteed capacity. We'll include SLA numbers in the pricing doc.
[00:07:49] [00:07:51] Sara: Any benchmark numbers for p95 on typical short chat (50 tokens)?
[00:07:55] Arjun: For rw-instruct on a standard hosted region we've seen p95 in the 200 600ms range depending on model and load; Dedicated tightens that with reserved GPU pools. We'll run your prompt set to get precise numbers.
[00:08:10] Jordan: Can we throttle by route or user?
[00:08:13] Arjun: Yes, per-route quotas and token budgets in Console; you can also set per-API-key limits.
[00:08:20] Lena: Next steps recap: we'll send pricing and security docs; Arjun will share streaming SDK examples + retry/idempotency snippets; ByteWave sends prompt set and traffic profile; schedule POC scoping.
[00:08:33] Maya: Sounds good, thanks.
[00:08:35] Lena: Thanks everyone  end call.

Note: transcript has occasional auto-corrections and speaker tag noise, e.g., "K-V cache" transcribed as "K-V kache" in a couple places.
